label: Primates

names.text: The item's given label is 'Primates'; no other common name for the order was checked.

sources.text: The lead gives Primates as an order of mammals, named by Carl Linnaeus in 1758. The item's given taxon is Primates (order).

about.text: Primates is an order of mammals with 376 to 524 living species, depending on the classification used. It has two suborders: Strepsirrhini (lemurs, galagos and lorises) and Haplorhini (tarsiers, monkeys and apes).

sources.text: The species range and the suborder lists are from the Primate article as fetched with WebFetch. The Haplorhini article was found through WebSearch result text, which described the same suborders and their contents.

gaps: No milk figure, yield or domestication applies to the order as a whole, and none was researched; the group record only places the order in the taxonomy. The Primate article was fetched only up to its first 100,000 characters, so no further detail was read.
